subject: management-of-business
title: Inventory Control: The Sawtooth Stock Chart

segments.say: Three levels govern the chart: maximum, reorder, buffer. Stock starts full at the maximum stock level of 1,000 units, the reorder level sits at 500 units, and the buffer stock is the 250-unit safety floor. Point at the three levels on your student notes before the stock line starts to fall.
questions: What are the three governing levels, and what is each level in units?
Which level is the safety floor stock should never fall below?

segments.say: Stock falls steadily - crossing the reorder level fires the order. Usage of 125 units a day pulls the line down in a straight slope, and the moment it crosses 500 units on day 4 the order is placed. Now try the timing questions on your worksheet.
questions: On which day does stock reach the reorder level, and how do you know?
Why is the order placed while 500 units remain?

segments.say: Through the lead time to the buffer - then the delivery jumps stock back up. The order takes 2 days to arrive and stock keeps falling meanwhile, down to the buffer of 250 units but never below it, and on day 6 the delivery jumps stock back to 1,000 units. Check the lead-time usage against your student notes before moving on.
questions: How much stock is used during the lead time?
What is the stock level at the moment the delivery lands?

segments.say: The sawtooth repeats: fall, reorder, wait, delivery, jump. The second cycle crosses the reorder level on day 10 and fires the next order. Keep the three levels, the 125 units a day usage rate and the 2-day lead time in view as you check your student notes and finish the exit ticket.
questions: On which day does the next order fire, and what triggers it?
What are the five beats of one sawtooth cycle, in order?
segments.watchFor: Reorder only when stock runs out, because buffer stock is spare stock that should never be touched and deliveries arrive straight away. Listen for students who call the buffer spare stock, or who wait for an empty shelf before ordering. Send them back to scene 3 and the lead time: Reorder when falling stock reaches the reorder level, not when it runs out: deliveries take a lead time to arrive, during which stock keeps falling, and the reorder level is set at buffer stock plus lead-time usage precisely so stock bottoms out at the buffer - never below it - just as the delivery lands.
